# DeployGuard

> DeployGuard is a distributed control plane for releasing feature flags and configuration changes safely across many application instances. It stages rollouts (for example 5%, 25%, 50%, 100%), watches health guardrails (error rate and p95 latency) for the users who receive the new variant, and automatically pauses or rolls back when a guardrail is breached.

This is a university mini project (Distributed Systems, BCE27PC01, Assignment 6). It runs as independent processes: several controllers (Java, gRPC + HTTP), several agents, PostgreSQL and RabbitMQ, deployed with Docker Compose or Kubernetes.

## Public pages
- [Overview](/): what the system does and its architecture
- [Documentation](/docs): architecture, algorithms, setup, troubleshooting, syllabus and lab mapping

## Distributed-systems mechanisms implemented
- Bully leader election between controller processes, with epochs
- Lamport and vector clocks on every message and event
- Expiring leases with monotonically increasing fencing tokens for mutual exclusion
- Wait-for-graph deadlock detection with youngest-victim resolution
- Chandy-Lamport snapshot over the broker channels (teaching demonstration)
- Cristian's clock synchronization between agents and controllers
- Heartbeat (beacon) failure detection with suspicion, not proof, of failure
- Retries with backoff, idempotent event handling, durable queues, reconnection and pull-based catch-up

## Notes for automated agents
- Operational pages (/dashboard, /flags, /rollouts, /agents, /topology, /experiments) and /api/* show live, unauthenticated control-plane state and are not meant for indexing.
- Traffic and faults shown in the dashboard are simulated and labelled as such.
